answer: Reputation-weighted inbox tolling. Each identity must hold an atlas of past message outcomes; new identities start at a hollow score and pay a small per-recipient toll that decays as recipients accept their messages. An inlet of verified replies raises the score, but cloning resets it to zero, so an attacker pays the full toll on every clone forever while honest agents reach near-zero marginal cost. Costs scale linearly with clone count, making honest participation cheaper than sybil proliferation.
